profile.org_note: Corporate (Arlington, TX) -> 14 internal homebuilding operating regions, each with a region president, a region CFO and region legal counsel -> 92 operating divisions (division president, controller, and the division's own land entitlement, acquisition and development staff) across 128 markets in 38 states; the 14 internal regions roll up into six reporting segments (Northwest, Southwest, South Central, Southeast, East, North), and the company does not publish the internal region map. Land deals are negotiated by the division, approved by the region president, then approved and funded at corporate by an executive officer: per the 2026 proxy the CEO (Romanowski) directly oversees six regions, the COO (Murray) six and the CFO (Wheat) two, each 'including approval of investments in land and lots'. No corporate head of land is publicly named. Finance contacts: CFO Bill Wheat (capital structure, financing, cash management), Treasurer Collin Dawson and SVP Real Estate Finance Jeff Tebeaux (both named only in Texas Comptroller officer reports). Majority-owned (about 62%) lot developer Forestar Group has its own officers and six regional offices and sells about 86% of its lots to D.R. Horton. The 2026 proxy also names Ryan and Reagan Horton (sons of the founder, 5%+ holders) as a related-party land seller and land banker to the company. The company does not publish the names or territories of its internal regions, so the region names shown here (West, South, East, North) are third-party labels. The 2025 Texas officer lists for DRHI, Inc. and D. R. Horton, Inc. name ten Region Presidents (Brundage, Davern, Etheridge, Farris, Hill, R. Horton, Lindhorst, Pentecost, Saltzberg, Whitehurst) for the 14 internal regions; third-party executive lists label Farris West, Rick Horton South and Hill East, and Horton and Lindhorst both sit on the Texas division entities. The six 10-K reporting segments are accounting roll-ups with no published leader.
profile.summary: Largest US homebuilder by closings every year since 2002: 84,202 homes closed and $33.0B consolidated revenue in fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-09-30), 92 divisions in 128 markets across 38 states, mostly entry-level and first move-up product at an average closing price of $363,600. Deliberately land-light: 570,600 lots owned and controlled at 2026-09-30, of which 77% (440,100) are controlled through purchase contracts and 68% of fiscal 2026 closings were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties; it owns about 62% of lot developer Forestar Group (NYSE: FOR), and its proxy states it routinely assigns land contracts to third-party lot developers and land bankers.
